b: Happy Thanksgiving to those who celebrate today. And while much of our audience is not US-based, we can all do ourselves a lot of good by stopping and thinking about something we’re thankful for.

This year, I’m thankful for the trends in illustration and advertising swinging back towards the obviously human and hand-made. I know it feels like every place we looks theres a bad AI generated flyer or terrible AI imposter “artist” but the tide of culture has absolutely started to turn back in favor of real artists in many industries.

Many of the forward thinking companies have made a stand for not using AI, and going back to hand-made crafts to make the point even clearer. Recent campaigns from Prada, elf, Apple, and others are highlighting the craft, time, effort, and human beings creating their art:
and if you pretend to be using handmade work and it’s suspected you’re not, the backlash is pretty swift:

And this hasn’t been just in advertising — many big publishers, both books and magazines, have been working to distance themselves from AI generated art. And yes, there have been a lot of missteps — but there’s also been a lot of redos and apologies. Unfortunately a lot of artists are lying about using AI, and as a result many publishers are starting to distance themselves from art that is even just the styles that AI emulates, just to be safe.

While there are still alarming trends of laying off artists in VisDev in favor of AI (looking at you, Marvel), it is a very positive sign that the longest stop motion feature ever made, Wildwood, just came out to wide acclaim and Grand Theft Auto 6, which relied heavily on real concept artists and real actors doing the motion capture, just made billions. These are projects that took a long time, and cost a lot of money, and were a real risk. It’s very heartening to see them pay off.

So this thanksgiving, I’m thankful for all the people out there that won’t accept AI slop. It’s now considered cheap, ugly, and the trends are swinging even further towards craft and obviously imperfect art making. And that’s good for real artists.
